Where it began

Salman Ali Agha was born in Lahore on 23 November 1993. He learned his cricket the long way, spending years with the Apollo Cricket Club in his home city before he got a first-class game, which finally came in February 2013.

He built his name on the domestic circuit with Southern Punjab, and along the way he had an adventure in Canada, where he made 218 runs in six games for the Edmonton Royals, the most by anyone in their side, at the first Global T20 tournament there.

The player

A right-hander who bats in the middle order and bowls off-spin, he had to be patient for his chance. Pakistan first called him into a Test squad in 2021, but his debut waited until the 2022 tour of Sri Lanka, where a patient 62 in a match his side lost showed what he could do. His first Test hundred followed that December, against New Zealand at Karachi, after the top order had been blown away.

In July 2023 he went back to Sri Lanka and was named Player of the Series, with 221 runs and three wickets as Pakistan won both Tests. At Galle he helped turn 101 for 5 into 461, and in the second Test he made an unbeaten 132. A year later, at Multan against England, another unbeaten hundred took him past 1,000 Test runs. By November 2026 he had played 28 Tests and made 1,708 runs at 36.34, with three hundreds and 12 fifties, plus 20 wickets and 42 catches.

What made him special

His gift was arriving when things had gone wrong and putting them right. Batting at seven or eight, he made a habit of rescuing Pakistan after collapses, sweeping and reverse-sweeping freely and keeping the scoreboard moving while the tail held on. In that Multan Test he added 65 for the ninth wicket with Sajid Khan to stretch the lead towards 300.

His off-spin was more of a useful extra than a weapon in Tests, at 61.15 a wicket, though plenty of part-time spinners would settle for 20 Test wickets and a best of 3 for 75.

Away from the middle

He became a leader in the white-ball teams, named vice-captain for one-day and Twenty20 cricket in 2024 and later captain of the Twenty20 side, which beat the West Indies 2-1 in a series played in Florida in 2025. His one-day batting flourished too: his 134 helped Pakistan chase down 352 against South Africa, their biggest successful chase in that format. He speaks Punjabi and Urdu.

And finally

After an ODI in South Africa in December 2024, where he took four wickets and saw the chase home with 82 not out, he was named Player of the Match. He gave the award to his partner Saim Ayub, who had made a hundred on debut. Some cricketers collect trophies; he gave one away.
